head: c3cd0ba3526ec83131b27ca9b22bc1297dcbe670
classification_reasons: Spec is tight: Flagged concerns is 'none', the one open question carried from intent.md (pre-check vs catch-and-reraise) is answered in spec.md's Open questions with a stated rationale (coding-standards rule 2), and Acceptance gives exact, checkable targets (the literal string 'whole must not be zero', the two named pre-existing tests still passing, pytest count 10, compileall/ruff healthy output).

Blast radius is small and below every routine threshold: the diff (cumulative through phase d) touches only sample_pkg/calc.py (percent's body), tests/test_calc.py (one new test function), and this change's own plan/spec/status/evidence files; no .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml in the diff; no sdlc.yaml risk_list item applies to an in-process arithmetic helper; percent's signature and return type are unchanged; no schema, migration or config surface exists in this project.

The changed branch is already covered by a pre-existing test: test_percent_zero_whole_raises (present before this change) already calls percent(1, 0) and asserts pytest.raises(ZeroDivisionError) over the exact branch the fix touches; the new test only tightens the existing assertion to the literal message, it does not open a new code path.
attempted: Intent: compared intent.md's Proposed outcome (message names 'whole', exception type ZeroDivisionError unchanged, divide's own message unchanged, a test written first and failing before the fix, three green targets) against the diff and the current sample_pkg/calc.py. percent now does try: return divide(part * 100, whole) / except ZeroDivisionError: raise ZeroDivisionError('whole must not be zero') from None, exactly as designed; divide() is byte-for-byte untouched (still 'if b == 0: raise ZeroDivisionError("b must not be zero")'). Nothing solves a nearby problem instead of this one.

Spec and plan: plan.md's Files-that-change order (tests/test_calc.py, then sample_pkg/calc.py) matches the actual commit order on this branch (reproducing test first, then the calc.py fix, confirmed via hook-log.jsonl's commit-phase invocations and the commit list). The catch-and-reraise-with-from-None shape plan.md's Risks flagged as the one easy way to depart from spec is implemented literally, including 'from None'. Flagged concerns in spec.md is 'none', so there was nothing left open to close at phase (d). No part of spec.md/plan.md is contradicted by the diff.

Proof: phase (d)'s own build.log/test.log/lint.log read '# <command> — deferred to the runner — <time>', which per the documented CI-deferred model (plugin 0.3.2 item 3b, issue #91) is not a proof gap — verifier.md states plainly that this session read, not ran, these targets, and the source tree is unchanged since phase (c), whose gate-c.json carries literal toolchain output: build exit 0 (no output), test exit 0 ('10 passed in 0.01s', collected 10 items including tests/test_calc.py's 9 and test_flag.py's 1), lint exit 0 ('All checks passed!'). evidence/failing-test.log is literal pytest output proving the new test fails pre-fix with exactly the message mismatch the fix resolves ('b must not be zero' vs 'whole must not be zero'), so the test is not vacuous. I did not re-run or cite any deterministic gate/skill check as a reason.

Blast radius: read the diff's full file list (sample_pkg/calc.py, tests/test_calc.py, plus this change's own plan.md/spec.md/status.yaml/evidence/*) and sdlc.yaml's risk_list; nothing outside changes/0015-*/** and the two source files is touched; no guardrail file appears anywhere in the diff; no risk-list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) applies.

Policies: coding-standards rule 2 (match the existing error-handling idiom) is followed — catch-and-reraise instead of a duplicate pre-check. Rule 4 (fail-first test for a behavior change) is satisfied and evidenced in failing-test.log. No new dependency is introduced. ux-conventions and data-conventions are correctly marked not applicable (library exception, no stored data). CLAUDE.md's 'Things Claude gets wrong' Layout-staleness note does not apply here: no public function was added or removed, and plan.md explicitly says so rather than staying silent.

Tests: test_percent_zero_whole_raises and test_divide_by_zero_raises are present in tests/test_calc.py unmodified (the diff hunk only inserts a new test function after the existing ones, with no removed or changed lines) — a fix-type change must not touch pre-existing tests, and it doesn't. The new test asserts the literal new string, not just the exception type, so it cannot pass with the pre-fix message still in place; failing-test.log demonstrates this directly.

Skip markers: grepped the diff for skip/xfail/pytest.ini exclusions — none added. gate-c.json's ratchets check already recorded skip_markers: [] and declared: []; nothing in the phase-d increment (status.yaml phase bump, evidence files, hook-log growth) adds a marker. plan.md needed no skip-marker declaration and has none.

Runner/session records: did not cite claude-b/c.json, run-b/c/d.json, gate-b/c.json, or adversarial-review-b/c.json as evidence for or against this diff; they were read only to understand phase sequencing and to confirm the source tree has not changed since phase (c)'s real green run, consistent with the diff itself showing no further sample_pkg/calc.py or tests/test_calc.py changes in phase (d).

Blast radius / guardrails: hook-log.jsonl's new entries (phase-d plumbing: gate start-run, set-phase, evidence collect, two git diff/push commands, and two shell_guard-blocked attempts to write a temp verification script via $TMPDIR, correctly blocked and retried against a literal /tmp path) show no .env read, no guardrail edit, and no bypass-permissions use.
